title: Do pieces that are not prime show what two numbers share?
description: Seventy two and one hundred forty four are split into pieces that are not prime, and the pieces look different. Splitting every piece into primes shows that the two numbers share two and three, and the highest common factor is seventy two.
teaching_notes: One idea: a split into pieces that are not prime cannot show what two numbers share, so split every piece into primes first. Watch for students who say two numbers have no common factor because their pieces look different.

video_script.why: The child has found the highest common factor from prime products and now meets two splits whose pieces are not prime, which hide the shared primes.
video_script.substitution: Split every piece into primes, compare the prime products, and keep the shared primes the smaller number of times.
video_script.anchor: The splits 72 = 6 × 12 and 144 = 8 × 18 written one under the other, with the pieces 6, 12, 8 and 18 shown.
video_script.payoff_line: No, they share common factors, and the highest common factor is seventy two

final_answer.value: No; the HCF of 72 and 144 is 72
final_answer.spoken: No, they share common factors, and the highest common factor is seventy two

never_show: the statement that the numbers share nothing, marked right
maths_rules: 6, 12, 8 and 18 are not prime, so these splits are not prime factorisations
primes in both are 2 and 3; 2 appears three times and four times, keep 3; 3 appears twice in both, keep 2

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, look at the pieces. Six, twelve, eight and eighteen are not primes.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>These splits are not prime factorisations, and they can hide shared primes.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, open the pieces of seventy two. Six is two times three, and twelve is two times two times three.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Together that is three twos and two threes.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, open the pieces of one hundred forty four. Eight is three twos, and eighteen is two times three times three.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Together that is four twos and two threes.
